scope: Data rows 36 through 70 inclusive; no empirical numeric values or E0 results reviewed.

rows.rationale: Boarding elapsed time may be an observed calibration target and may also emerge from downstream bed/transfer processes. Treat it as a generated input only for an explicitly modeled residual boundary delay; keep observed boarding anchors and censoring separate to avoid fitting and replaying the same interval.
rows.replacement: Define the event anchors and modeled residual boundary explicitly; identify the observed boarding interval as target-only unless the residual delay is the generative component. Retain seconds/source precision and convert to ticks only under a separately declared C0 resolution and rounding rule.

rows.rationale: A single transit duration conflates aggregate macro travel delay with micro spatial movement. Observed transit can be a target; micro transit should be generated from route distance and speed so the same travel interval is not also sampled as a duration.
rows.replacement: Declare mode-specific semantics: macro aggregate transit duration distribution, or micro route distance plus walking speed and interruptions; observed transit anchors remain separate calibration targets. Preserve source precision and use the C0-declared checked tick conversion.

Timezone alone does not specify recurring local roster behavior at daylight-saving transitions or how source precision is represented. Absolute instants must normalize to UTC, while recurring local schedules need zone and transition policy.
rows.replacement: For instants require an explicit IANA timezone/offset, preserve source precision, normalize to UTC, and declare ambiguous/nonexistent-local-time handling. For recurrence retain local zone, recurrence rule, and DST transition policy; intervals use ED clock units and declared tick conversion.

rows.rationale: Break schedules have the same timezone/DST ambiguity as rosters; breaks also affect availability intervals rather than event durations alone.
rows.replacement: Use the roster schedule contract: explicit IANA zone/offset, preserved precision, UTC normalization for instants, explicit ambiguous/nonexistent-time policy for local recurrence, and a separately declared interval/tick conversion.

rows.rationale: Local timezone is insufficient to resolve DST folds/gaps; retain effective staffing intervals distinctly from observed staffing records and from outcome metrics.
rows.replacement: Represent count delta and effective interval separately; require explicit zone/offset and DST policy for local schedules, preserve source precision, normalize instants to UTC, and declare checked conversion for interval boundaries.

Calendar schedules need explicit recurrence and DST semantics; absolute source precision and local zone cannot be inferred.
rows.replacement: Require explicit timezone/offset and precision for instants; for recurring calendars preserve IANA zone and recurrence plus ambiguous/nonexistent-time policy. Normalize instants to UTC and declare interval-to-tick conversion.

rows.rationale: Outage intervals need the same source timezone, DST, precision and interval conversion contract as calendars; observed outage records are evidence/input provenance, not a model outcome.
rows.replacement: Require explicit timezone/offset and source precision, explicit DST policy for recurring local schedules, UTC normalization for instants, and declared checked tick conversion for interval boundaries.

rows.rationale: Reservation intervals require explicit timezone/DST/precision semantics. Resource reservations are model inputs; observed occupancy or reservation timestamps can be targets only under separately mapped event definitions.
rows.replacement: Require explicit timezone/offset and precision, recurrence/DST policy when local time recurs, UTC normalization, and declared checked conversion; preserve reservation events separately from occupancy targets.

The unit is suitable, but elapsed interruption/suspension time can be confused with active switching work. Calibration against observed task gaps without event decomposition risks counting queue or interruption delay twice.
rows.replacement: Define switching overhead as active work attributable to context/task switching, in seconds with source precision; keep queue, suspension and resumption elapsed intervals separate as observations/targets. Convert through the C0-declared checked tick rule.

A trip count is an exposure/event count, not interchangeable with equipment capacity. Aggregated observed trip counts need a declared observation window and denominator before serving as targets.
rows.replacement: Type trip events/counts separately from equipment capacity; declare count window/exposure and event mapping for observed targets. Keep capacity as a separate non-negative integer resource input.

The route rule allows time leaves but does not define occurrence, duration, or whether an interruption is part of travel time; this can double count route delay.
rows.replacement: Separate interruption occurrence/cause policy from interruption duration and movement progress; explicit time leaves use seconds and C0-declared tick conversion. Preserve observed interruption event timestamps/lineage as targets, not as silent generated defaults.

rows.rationale: The row is expressly deferred and excluded. There is no approved congestion mechanism or observation mapping in the reviewed C0 scope, so no calibration role or tick semantics can be accepted now.
rows.replacement: Keep deferred; require separately reviewed extension scope, measurable congestion events/exposure, event mapping, units, and identifiable target/input roles before activation.

rows.rationale: A patience threshold is a latent generative abandonment rule, while observed queue time before abandonment is an outcome with censoring. Equating observed wait or completed waits with patience would bias calibration.
rows.replacement: Define as latent time-to-abandon threshold or hazard with explicit conditioning; map abandonment event and last-observed/censoring separately. Do not use non-abandoning completed waits as patience values. Preserve seconds/source precision and use declared tick conversion.
